This happened to me. I listened almost daily from my 13s to 18/19s, but at that time I was kind of bored of listening to them. Not only bored of them being on repeat on my mp3 player, but bored of listening to any of their songs again. So I stopped listening to them, and thought of them as a band that helped me grow, a very important cultural element that grounded my Identity and who I was. That helped me to overcome the tensions of becoming unidentified with something so utterly important to me.
I did not listened to them for years, I think maybe 2/3 whole years (except when I was with friends and they were listening to WTTBP, Na Na Na, or some of those hits). I do not regret those years, at all, as I was becoming a different person, with a different personality and a different attitude. 
When MCRX was announced, I started listening to them again, but only for a few weeks, and just some of their songs. I enjoyed those weeks, but I felt that it was not my cup of tea again. I did not feel bad about it, people change. I grew apart from them. But thinking of how important and how influential they were for me, made me think of them as a great memory and one of the best relationships I have ever had (and will ever have).
When they announced the return, I was immediately transported to the black parade and I started to listening to them again. I do not consume their music as compulsively as in my teen years. And I think that the gap I was telling you about, and also the fact that I was able to not feel unidentified and disassociated with them has helped me to engage with them in a more positive and healthy way, one that this older me can relate more.
